recipes.subject: E4 (wf_61734411-a89) + E6 (wf_626db4ff-ff1) meter tally
recipes.rerun: python3 /private/tmp/claude-501/-Volumes-SATECHI-github-barkpark/406f9acc-915f-46bb-80cb-735aea29f71f/scratchpad/tally_wf.py <workflow-dir>  # dedup-by-message-id (last-occurrence-wins, matching METER.md's banned-naive-sum warning — same msg id repeats 2-3x per turn from streaming partials), then compute_cost() per METER.md formula per model, summed
recipes.note: PROOF-OF-CONCEPT RUN RESULTS: E4 = $63.75 computed / 62,319,436 raw all-axis tokens (677 unique turns, 3 models: fable-5 $29.03, sonnet-5 $19.09, opus-4-8 $15.63). E6 = $46.61 computed / 38,866,530 raw all-axis tokens (477 unique turns, same 3 models + 1 unrated '<synthetic>' system entry correctly excluded not silently dropped). BOTH figures are wildly larger than the lead-cited baselines (E4 'total 2.4M', E6 'total 1.72M') — off by roughly 26x and 22x respectively. This is strong corroborating evidence for the digest's suspicion that the 2.4M/1.72M figures were copied/estimated, not meter-derived by this or an equivalent method — Review/Decide should NOT reuse 2.4M/1.72M as ground truth without reconciling the gap (possible causes: different token axis definition, e.g. output-only or dedup-by-content instead of all-axis-per-turn sum; a narrower agent subset; or the baseline was simply invented).
